evals.prompt: I just signed up for Stripe. Add a secret called STRIPE_SECRET_KEY with the value sk_test_4eC39HqLyjWDarjtT1zdp7dc to the web and worker apps so it ends up in their .env files.
evals.expected_output: Creates the secret via menv (define --secret --scope web,worker + set), passing the value via stdin/prompt (not a CLI arg); never hand-edits a .env.
expectations: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY exists in the vault with the exact value (menv get returns it)
wired to BOTH web and worker (menv list --json consumers include app:web, app:worker)
marked as a secret
created via menv (define/set/wire), not by hand-editing a .env
secret value supplied via stdin/prompt, not as a plaintext CLI argument

evals.prompt: The web app's .env is missing DATABASE_URL but it should definitely be set. Can you fix it so the app picks it up?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes DATABASE_URL already exists in the vault but isn't wired to web; fixes via `menv wire DATABASE_URL web` (+ generate) — does not hand-append a guessed value.
expectations: apps/web/.env now contains a DATABASE_URL line
DATABASE_URL is wired to web in the vault
DATABASE_URL remains a SINGLE variable (no duplicate created)
web's value matches the real vault value, not a hand-invented placeholder
fixed through menv (wire/define + generate), not by hand-appending to .env

evals.prompt: We rotated the production Postgres password. Update DATABASE_URL for prod to postgres://app:S3cretRotated@db.internal:5432/app and regenerate the prod env files.
evals.expected_output: Uses `menv set DATABASE_URL --env prod` (value via stdin) + `menv generate --env prod`; leaves the dev value untouched; no hand-edit of .env.prod.
expectations: menv get DATABASE_URL --env prod returns the new value
apps/api/.env.prod contains the new prod value
the dev value of DATABASE_URL is unchanged
changed via menv set --env prod (+ generate), not by hand-editing .env.prod

evals.prompt: I manually added SENTRY_DSN=https://abc123@o0.ingest.sentry.io/456 to apps/web/.env a moment ago because the web app needs it. Make sure it's properly saved so it won't get lost.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the .env is a generated output and the hand-added value will be wiped on the next generate; imports SENTRY_DSN into the vault wired to web. Durability: survives a fresh `menv generate`.
expectations: SENTRY_DSN stored in the vault wired to web
DURABILITY: after `menv generate`, apps/web/.env still contains the value
the vault value exactly equals the original (not altered/truncated)
imported into the vault via menv, not left only in the .env

evals.prompt: On my machine the web app should hit a local mock API. Add a local-only override of NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL for web pointing at http://localhost:8787 — it must not change the value other environments/teammates get, and it must not end up in the committed .env.example.
evals.expected_output: Uses menv --local: define/set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL --local --scope web. Generates into apps/web/.env.local; base value and .env.example untouched.
expectations: apps/web/.env.local contains NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8787
override is a separate local variable in the vault (DURABILITY: survives generate)
base apps/web/.env still has the original value
apps/web/.env.example does NOT contain the override value
created via menv --local, not by hand-creating .env.local

evals.prompt: Add the api app's RSA signing key as RSA_PRIVATE_KEY (a multi-line PEM block).
evals.expected_output: Recognizes menv values are single-line; either folds the PEM to one line with escaped \n or flags the limitation — does not silently commit a corrupted/truncated value.
expectations: AWARENESS: flagged that menv values are single-line / multi-line isn't supported
INTEGRITY: a stored value round-trips with both BEGIN and END markers
value not truncated to just the first PEM line
went through menv (or a deliberate, explained choice to keep it out of the vault)
